evidence.curator_note: Substrate as drawn: the 2-ethylhexanal molecular ion, labelled 'm/z 128' under the structure. The skeleton is printed as C2H5-CH(H)-CH2-CH(C2H5)-CHO with the gamma hydrogen on C4 drawn EXPLICITLY, an aldehyde H on C1, and '+.' printed above the carbonyl oxygen. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the charge and odd electron are written on the oxygen exactly where the page prints them, [CH:1]=[O+:7], not carried only in the JSON fields. Middle channel. The book draws ONE arrow carrying THREE labels -- 'rH' above, then 'alpha' and '- C2H4' -- straight to the structure it labels 'm/z 100'; no intermediate is drawn and Book draws 0 arc(s) for it, so all five moves are curator-supplied. WHICH HYDROGEN, and why this is not the C4 gamma-H: the printed m/z 100 product is a STRAIGHT six-carbon chain, C2H5-CH2-CH2-CH(•)-CH= O(+)H, with the radical dot alpha to the carbonyl. That structure forces the reading: the migrating hydrogen is the gamma' H of the ETHYL BRANCH (map 11, on C9, which is gamma to the carbonyl by the path C1-C2-C8-C9), and the branch then leaves as ethylene by beta-cleavage of the C2-C8 bond -- i.e. the three printed labels are one complete McLafferty rearrangement running on the ethyl branch rather than on the main chain. MASS BOOKKEEPING that settles it: C8H16O (16 H) -> C6H12O (12 H) + C2H4 (4 H). Taking the O-H hydrogen from C4 instead would leave C4 with one H and give C6H11O+, which is not 100 and not what is drawn. The C4 gamma-H drawn on the molecular ion belongs to the OTHER channel (IMS9-EQ9.25b) and is therefore left implicit in this record. MS CONTEXT: this page prints no ionisation conditions, so 70 eV EI is the corpus house default and is disclosed here rather than read off the page (the same treatment as IMS9-EQ9.19a/b and IMS8-EQ8.114). Figure 9.8 on printed p247 is the 2-ethylhexanal spectrum and would supply abundances, but it is NOT on this page and the scheme itself prints no percentage, so convention F forbids importing an intensity: every peak_assignment here carries status 'proposed' with no relative_intensity.

evidence.curator_note: Arrow labelled 'alpha' from m/z 100 to m/z 57. The radical on C2 drives cleavage of the C3-C4 bond with formation of the C2=C3 pi bond, expelling the propyl radical C3H7. (43) and giving the same C3H5O+ ion (m/z 57) that the other branch reaches. Book draws 2 arc(s), both on the m/z 100 structure: a fishhook whose tail is on the C3-C4 bond and whose head points down into the forming C2=C3 region, and a fishhook from the printed radical dot below C2 curving up into that same region. Move <3>, carrying the second C3-C4 electron away with the propyl radical, is implicit (not drawn).

data/mechanisms/rule_index.json has NO chapter-9 entries at all (by_equation covers only 4.x and 8.x), so any link is inferred rather than indexed. *** VERIFIED, and it independently corroborates this record's reading of the composite arrow. *** hTransition_unsaturated (IMS_bookCover.py:40, '[H]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5{=}[_A+.]6 >> [C.]2[C]3[C]4[C]5{=}[_A+]6[H]1', _A = O) embeds on the molecular ion TWICE. The second embedding, maps (9,8,2,1,7), is precisely the ethyl-branch gamma'-hydrogen that this record argues the composite 'rH, alpha, -C2H4' arrow must use -- i.e. the rule set finds the branch gamma-position independently of the mass argument given in the step note. (The first embedding, maps (4,3,2,1,7), is the main-chain gamma-H that drives IMS9-EQ9.25b.) By contrast hTransition_unsaturated_alpha gives ZERO matches on this record's m/z 100 ion, which is correct and expected: after the ethylene loss the radical sits ALPHA to the carbonyl (C2), not gamma, so the 1,4-relationship that rule requires no longer exists. Step 2 therefore has no counterpart in that rule.
